sentences.text: Based on the holotype, this animal was estimated to be about 3 meters long and 1.5 meters tall, though it may have grown larger as the specimen was immature.
Carnufex was among the largest crocodylomorphs of the Triassic period.
The creature exhibits a mix of features found in both crocodylomorphs and their distant ancestors like the reptile Postosuchus.
It is highly autapomorphic, possessing many unique features that distinguish it from its close relatives.
The premaxillary teeth were slender, serrated, and recurved, while the maxillary teeth were serrated and knife-like with a significantly convex front edge and a slightly concave rear side.
The posterior process of the maxilla was circular in cross-section at the front but deepened and thinned towards the rear.
The antorbital fenestra, a very large and elongated triangular hole, was a prominent feature of the skull.
The outer surface of the jugal bone was covered with pits and ridges.
The cervical neural arch was a complex bone featuring nine laminae and twelve fossae.
The humerus was short with a constricted shaft.
Rough areas and bumps on the top of the head suggest that decorative features may have developed there.
The snout is long and narrow, with longer, serrated-edged teeth at the front contrasting with those at the back.
The genus Carnufex was first described in 2015 by Zanno et al. with the species name Carnufex carolinensis, which translates to "Carolina butcher".
The holotype specimen NCSM 51228 was discovered in the middle-to-upper part of the Pekin Formation in North Carolina, USA.
The holotype includes most of the skeleton: a partial skull, vertebrae, ribs, and an upper arm bone.
Carnufex was the largest known carnivore in its ecosystem, but this might be due to sampling bias hiding larger predators like rauisuchids.
Carnufex is classified as a primitive crocodylomorph, belonging to a group of suchians more derived than Rauisuchidae.
Phylogenetic analysis suggests Carnufex is the most basal crocodylomorph, sharing this position with an unnamed genus.
A phylogenetic analysis included basal taxa like Mesosuchus and derived ones like Protosuchus and the modern Alligator.
Fossils of Carnufex date to the Carnian age of the Late Triassic, approximately 231 million years ago, with a time range from 237 to 227.3 million years ago.
Carnufex was an extinct crocodylomorph that lived in North America during the Late Triassic.
